analogy.boundary: Passing the form check only lets the declaration be used; it says nothing about whether the description of the goods is accurate.

maps.analogy: a declaration that clears the goods
maps.doctrine: a rule document with the force to govern

maps.analogy: the supporting paperwork that must come with it
maps.doctrine: the evidence the rule must produce
the declared statement of what it does not cover

maps.analogy: the convincing letter that clears nothing

analogy.text: A customs declaration clears goods only when it passes the form check, comes with its supporting paperwork and states what it does not vouch for. A convincing letter describing the shipment clears nothing.

reader.counterexample: A persuasive standard written in prose is treated as binding because it sounds authoritative, though no parser accepted its structure and it lists no evidence requirements or limits.
reader.does_not_prove: A document that passes the parser is well formed; whether its content is complete or correct is a separate question.

example.text: The executable doctrine grammar component accepts a standard only when its structure parses and its evidence requirements and limits statement are present, and rejects a standard written in prose that claims authority without that structure.

reader.governs: Whether a rule document may govern, or is only something to read.
reader.plain: A rule can govern only when it passes a fixed format check and lists the evidence it must produce and what it leaves out. A well-written paragraph on its own is something to read.
reader.potential_misread: That passing the format check means the rule fully covers its subject, when the check looks only at the rule's structure.
reader.refuses: Prose claiming the force of an executable rule.
reader.requires: Acceptance by the grammar parser, a list of the evidence the rule must produce and a declared statement of what it does not cover.
reader.why_it_matters: A confident paragraph is not enforced as a rule just because it sounds authoritative.

Lineage: formal languages, type systems, operational semantics, Hoare
contracts.

Route: recorded as strongly witnessed by `executable_doctrine_grammar`,
`standards_meta_diagnostics` and all public paper modules. The tests reject a
prose standard that claims executable authority, and a claim that passing the
grammar check means more than it does.

Anti-axiom: prose claims the authority of an executable rule.
data.title: Executable grammar before doctrine authority
